rationale: Verb in line 12 governing 'in many days and months walking until they reach (him).' Context demands a temporal-extension verb. Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲱϥⲧ̄ 'be wearied, prolonged' or related stem. Tentative; flagged for parallels.
Lycopolitan compound preposition ϩⲓ-ⲧ-ϩⲏ 'in-the-front,' standard Coptic spatial term. Used in line 8 of the comitatus-members who walk before the king.
Verbal idiom ⲣ̄- ('do') + ϣⲁⲣⲡ ('first') + ⲁⲣⲁϩ ('to him') = 'do-first toward him' = 'precede him.' Standard Coptic precedence-construction.
Lycopolitan ϩⲓ-ⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'on-the-back' = behind. Standard spatial preposition; pair-partner with ⲍⲓⲧⲍⲏ 'in front.'
Greek loanword στράτευμα 'army.' Used here for the king's military retinue, paired with ⲡⲉϩⲕⲟⲙⲓⲧⲁⲧⲟⲛ 'his comitatus' as the imperial-military escort.

Greek loanwords ἀποδημία (noun) and ἀποδημέω (verb). Already partially attested in glossary as ⲁⲡⲟⲍⲏⲙⲓ; this kephalaion uses standard Greek-orthography ⲁⲡⲟⲇⲏⲙ-. Central technical term: the comitatus's journey from the king's gate-place to wherever he sets out.

Coptic ⲙⲉⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'sign, mark, manner.' Here in 'the manner of the journey to the country which he wishes' — the structured pattern of the king's progress, allegorically applied to the catechumen's progress.
